messages:
irina: FYI Acme (vpc-prod-acme) opened a support ticket — since ~09:12 PST they get intermittent 403s when our private nodes call their KMS-backed key wrapper. Also their audit logs are missing for those time ranges and billing attribution shows 0 usage for the dedicated pool. Can we triage? :thinking_face:

devon: Copy. Can you drop repro steps and any tcpdump or curl output? We should confirm whether this is a network egress problem (NAT / firewall / proxy) or a KMS auth regression.

samir: Repro steps from the customer's engineer: from a control container on vpc-prod-acme run `curl -v https://kms.prod.redwood.internal/v1/keys/our-key:encrypt` with their service token. They see: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden and headers `x-redwood-kms-code: AccessDenied` but our control-plane logs show no corresponding audit record for many of those requests. Trying to reproduce now.

samir: Quick curl output (sanitized):

```
> curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" https://kms.prod.redwood.internal/v1/keys/our-key:encrypt
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Date: Tue, 11 Feb 2025 16:12:03 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
x-request-id: abcdef12345
x-redwood-kms-code: AccessDenied
Content-Length: 172

{ "error": "access denied: key not found or unauthorized" }
```

maria: Important detail: customer is on Private (VPC) with our proxy NAT + SGs. We recently tightened the default egress SG in the hardened profile — it denies ephemeral egress to external IP ranges unless explicitly allowed. KMS calls should be allowed to our KMS subnet via the NAT gateway or a VPC endpoint. Can you share `ip route`, `iptables -L`, and the ENI IP the node uses?

irina: Got `ip route` from one node and a short tcpdump. IPs redacted: ENI 10.12.34.56, KMS VIP 10.99.88.77. Route table points at nat-gtw-01 for 0.0.0.0/0, but the node's source IP is getting SNATed to the wrong IP (10.12.34.99) which is not in the NAT allowlist for the KMS ACLs. tcpdump shows TLS handshake then an immediate RST. snippet:

```
09:12:03.123456 IP 10.12.34.56.57234 > 10.99.88.77.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
09:12:03.223456 IP 10.12.34.56.57234 > 10.99.88.77.443: Flags [P.], seq 12346:12398, ack 1, length 52
09:12:03.323456 IP 10.99.88.77.443 > 10.12.34.56.57234: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 0, length 0
```

maria: That RST + SNAT mismatch could explain the 403 + missing audit logs (KMS sees unknown client IP and rejects before logging). Also billing attribution could break if requests aren't successfully authenticated/accepted by control plane. :exclamation:

devon: Who changed the hardened SG list? @maria do we have a config drift or recent policy rollout note?

maria: I pushed a global hardened default SG change last week (was rolled to a subset of Private tenants for audit testing). Looks like Acme was included by mistake via a tag rule. I've opened a rollback but we need immediate mitigation.

oncall-bot: Incident checklist: if customer impact >1 customer / production, open incident and page platform oncall. (automated)

irina: Impact: single high-value customer, production traffic impacted intermittently. They report ~30% of KMS calls failing since 09:12. Recommend paging.

devon: Agreed — paging platform oncall. In the meantime, workaround: add a temporary SG egress allow for the node SNAT IP (10.12.34.99) to the KMS VIP (10.99.88.77) port 443 and revert the hardened rule for that tenant. Can we get exact ACL updates?

maria: I'll push an emergency ACL to allow SNAT range 10.12.34.96/28 to the KMS VIP on 443 and rollback the tag-based inclusion for Acme. Deploying now, ETA ~6 mins.

logs-bot: Found relevant VPC Flow Log samples (filtered):
```
- src=10.12.34.56 dst=10.99.88.77 sport=57234 dport=443 action=REJECT
- src=10.12.34.99 dst=10.99.88.77 sport=57234 dport=443 action=ACCEPT
```
Note: NAT translation occurs; some packets hit REJECT because SNAT not in KMS ACL.

samir: After temporary SG change I see 200s again from one node. Customer confirms partial recovery. We still need to validate audit log backfill for the missing window and why some requests were accepted while others rejected (looks environmental: some pods used a different SNAT IP).

maria: Postmortem action items I propose: 1) Add unit test to tenant-tagging automation to avoid accidental inclusion in hardened rollouts, 2) ensure NAT SNAT ranges are included in KMS ACLs automatically via discovery, 3) add guardrail to detect when control-plane audit logs are missing for a tenant (alert if request success rate vs audit ingestion deviates).

irina: Also confirm billing attribution pipeline — add a check that flags zero usage for active reserved pools. I will open a billing ticket to reconcile charges for the affected window.

devon: For now, close loop with customer: confirm all nodes connect, share tcpdump + flowlogs + ACL diffs we applied, and ask them to run a quick smoke: `for i in {1..20}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://kms.prod.redwood.internal/v1/keys/our-key:encrypt; done` and paste results.

irina: Will send updates to Acme and include rollback diff. Thanks all — keep this thread for postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
